verifiedSourceCorrections.finding: Universal two's-complement and eight-bit-int claims persist. In the C17 contract, optionB's minimum signed range is the portable guarantee; sizeof(int) is not fixed. Exact intN_t, when provided, does promise its stated width and two's-complement representation.
Always compile-time sizeof is too broad: distinguish VLA operands and non-VLA unevaluated operands; result type size_t.

Automatic indeterminate int32_t must not be assigned an invented garbage output. Static-duration arithmetic objects receive zero initialization. Java local definite-assignment rules do not mean all Java declarations get default values.

Truth is a scalar value comparison against zero, not a bit-pattern test. IEEE negative zero is false despite its sign bit; NaN converts to true. Aggregates are not arbitrary scalar conditions. Null pointer representations need not be all-zero bits.

Side-effect repetition is branch-dependent. The argument occurs once in the comparison and again only if its corresponding arm is selected. Distinguish repeat evaluation from unsequenced modification conflicts.

typedef is an alias, not a new distinct scalar type. const qualification does not make a C17 object an integer constant expression. Macro replacement is token-based, not unrestricted substring replacement.

originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.contract: CHAR_BIT=8, unsigned char maximum255, int represents0..255
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.example: unsigned char b=255; compare b+1>b and (unsigned char)(b+1)>b
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.derivation: First, b promotes to int255, so b+1 is int256 and comparison is true. In the second expression, the explicit unsigned-char conversion reduces256 modulo256 to0; comparison0>255 is false. For b+=2, addition produces int257 and assignment converts to unsigned char1. Separate operation type from stored type.

MIN(3,i++) first compares3<4, increments i to5, selects constant3, and yields3 with i=5. MIN(5,i++) compares5<4, increments i to5, selects the second arm, then yields its old value5 and increments i to6. MIN(i++,i++) has conflicting unsequenced modifications during the condition and has no valid numerical trace.

originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.contract: Unsigned32-bit n, positive unsigned divisor d
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.derivation: Write n=qd+r with0<=r<d. Then ceil(n/d)=q+(r!=0), implemented n/d+(n%d!=0). If d=1 then remainder0 prevents an increment of maximum quotient. For n=4294967295,d=2, correct result2147483648; (n+d-1)/d wraps its numerator to0 and returns0. Explain mathematical ceiling before machine evaluation.

originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.example: int s=-1; unsigned int u=1; inspect 1?s:u
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.derivation: The conditional arithmetic result has unsigned-int type even though only s is selected. Its selected value converts to4294967295. Branch selection cannot bypass the common-type conversion. Compare (long)-1<1U under explicitly declared LP64 and LLP64: true when64-bit long represents every unsigned32 value; false when32-bit long cannot, because both operands convert to unsigned long.

originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.example: For integer n=7,d=4 compare (double)(n/d), (double)n/d; for positive physical radius r inspect G*m1*m2/r*r
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.derivation: The first division occurs in int, giving1 before conversion to1.0; the second converts an operand before division and gives1.75. Left-associative division/multiplication parses the physical expression as (((G*m1)*m2)/r)*r, cancelling r mathematically instead of dividing by r squared. Use /(r*r), and independently audit the declared types/ranges of the denominator multiplication.

originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.example: Original assignments a=7,b=11; t=a; b=t; a=b
originalReasoningProblemsForAuthoring.derivation: Trace(7,11,7) then(7,7,7) then(7,7,7): this is not a swap. The correct temporary swap copies old b into a before assigning t into b. Compare C expression90<=grade<=100: relational operators return int0/1, so its parsed left comparison is always<=100; Java instead rejects comparison of Boolean with integer. Never turn Java diagnostics into C output.

questionDesignAdvice: Every trace should state language/version, integer model and initial state, then annotate parse tree, promotions, common type, mathematical value, storage conversion and sequencing. Classify undefined behavior before simulating.

Medium/hard questions should change the decisive assumption, not only numeric constants: LP64/LLP64, cast before/after arithmetic, non-VLA/VLA sizeof, automatic/static storage, integer modulo/real conversion, conditional arm type and macro branch.

For binary rational termination, reduce numerator/denominator; termination in base2 requires denominator a power of2. Exact representability additionally requires significand precision and exponent-range bounds; termination alone is insufficient.
Guard mathematical formulas against undefined or invalid domains and intermediate range overflow. A wider destination type does not retroactively widen an already-evaluated narrower operation.
C17 enum identifiers, const objects and macros need distinct constant-expression questions; all answers should explain both successful and rejected forms.
Do not execute UB examples and treat a compiler run as a scientific answer. For defined examples, execution can corroborate a derivation only under the matching declared model.
